description: The figure presents three pie charts showing the distribution of four problem-category combinations under a Zero-Shot setting, separated by difficulty levels labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” with 4 slices in each pie. In the “easy” pie, the slices are N+K+ (teal) at about 55.4%, N−K+ (yellow) at about 38.3%, N−K− (orange) at about 4.6%, and N+K− (red) at about 1.7%, with percentage labels printed inside the slices. In the “medium” pie, N+K+ (teal) is about 58.8%, N−K+ (yellow) about 35.4%, N−K− (orange) about 4.0%, and N+K− (red) about 1.8%, again with internal percentage labels. In the “hard” pie, N−K− (orange) is about 37.9%, N−K+ (yellow) about 37.3%, N+K+ (teal) about 18.1%, and N+K− (red) about 6.7%, with percentages shown inside the slices. A legend on the right maps colors to the four labels (N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, N+K−), and none of the slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized; within each pie, the slices appear arranged with the largest segments occupying the most prominent arcs but not in a strictly consistent ordering across all three charts.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of problem categories labeled as 'easy,' 'medium,' and 'hard' under Zero-Shot settings, with four segments in each chart. For the 'easy' category, the largest segment is 'N+K+' in teal, accounting for approximately 55.4%, followed by 'N−K+' in yellow at 38.3%. The 'medium' category shows a similar trend, with 'N+K+' comprising 58.8% and 'N−K+' at 35.4%. In the 'hard' category, 'N−K−' in orange is the largest segment at 47.9%, followed by 'N−K+' in yellow at 37.3%. Notably, the proportion of 'N+K−' in red remains consistent across all categories, stabilizing at around 1.7% for 'easy' and 'medium,' and increasing slightly to 6.7% for 'hard.' These charts highlight a decline in 'N+K+' as difficulty increases, while 'N−K−' exhibits a sharp rise in the 'hard' category.
